title: Develop Streetlight Repair Prioritization Matrix / Non-Emergency Streetlight Repair Request / Develop / Implement
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the Council instruct the Bureau of Street Lighting, with assistance from the Chief Legislative Analyst as needed, to develop and implement a transparent, objective Streetlight Repair Prioritization Matrix for all non-emergency streetlight repair requests. I FURTHER MOVE that the prioritization matrix, modeled after the City's Sidewalk Repair Program, prioritize outages located: • Within or adjacent to single-family and multi-family residential neighborhoods; • Near parks, schools, libraries, recreation centers, senior centers, and transit stops; • Along high-pedestrian corridors, including Safe Routes to School; • In locations with documented public safety concerns, including higher rates of pedestrian or vehicle collisions or crime. I FURTHER MOVE that the prioritization matrix assign lower priority to routine, non-emergency outages located primarily within commercial and industrial corridors, while preserving the Bureau's existing practice of immediately responding to electrical hazards and other emergency conditions. I FURTHER MOVE that the Bureau report to Council within 90 days with the proposed prioritization methodology, implementation timeline, and any resources or policy changes necessary to implement the prioritization system.
